extracted.intended_audience: Researchers invited as co-applicants on SSHRC Insight Grants (October 2025 competition)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for co-applicants accepting an invitation to participate on an SSHRC Insight Grants application, including what to attach, formatting and page limits, how to verify the CV, and optional career interruption documentation. Focused on completing the Accept Invitation form and its required attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach verified CV when accepting invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: When you accept the invitation, the system will attach a copy of your verified CV to the form. You must return to the My Portfolio screen, click Verify, and verify and correct the data until the Verification Report indicates successful verification. Click “Refresh CV” for the particular form after making changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The status on your Portfolio will change from “In Progress” to “Verified.” At this stage your CV is part of the full application. You can preview the form and CV and print them in PDF format by clicking “Preview.” When the applicant submits the application, the status will change to “Submitted.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Must attach electronic research contributions document
rubrics_metrics.description: As a co-applicant, you must attach to the Accept Invitation form an electronic copy of your research contributions. Research contributions content must address the Capability evaluation criteria listed in the funding opportunity description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You have four pages in total to cover the specified sections (see separate rubric entries). If you do not attach this document, the Accept Invitation form will not be verified and the application will be incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and technical requirements for attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments must follow specified requirements for margins, font size, page length and file size or the Accept Invitation form will not be verified and the entire application may be incomplete or ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific technical requirements: do not exceed 500 kB; use minimum 12-point Times New Roman font; have at least 3/4" (1.87 cm) margins; be single-spaced with no more than 6 lines of type per inch; use page size 8.5" x 11" (216 mm x 279 mm). An error message will appear if file does not meet required specifications. Recommendation: after attaching click “View attached file” to ensure correct file and not corrupted. Failure to follow requirements may render the application ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research contributions — overall order and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The attachment must be presented in this order: Relevant research contributions over the last six years; Other research contributions; Most significant career research contributions; Contributions to training. Maximum four pages for the research contributions attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must cover the sections listed as applicable within the four-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant research contributions (last six years) — scope and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline your research contributions within six years of the application deadline. In the case of co-applicants claiming Career interruptions and special circumstances, you may include publications drawn from your most recent periods of research activity to an overall total of six years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details about contributions as appropriate (see marking SSHRC-funded items, role in co-authored works, student authorship, bibliographic notices, translations, theses for recent graduates, grouping and ordering by category and most recent first).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark SSHRC-funded contributions and student authors
rubrics_metrics.description: In the left margin, identify with an asterisk (*) research contributions that resulted from previous SSHRC support. Identify each student author with a plus sign (+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also specify your role in co-authored publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify role in co-authored publications
rubrics_metrics.description: For co-authored publications you must specify your role (e.g., author contributions, lead author, co-author).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps reviewers assess individual contribution to co-authored outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide complete bibliographic notices for published contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: For published contributions, provide complete bibliographic notices (including co-authors, title, publisher, journal, volume, date of publication and number of pages) as they appear in the original publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For publications in languages other than French or English, provide a translation of the title and the name of the publication. For recent graduates, list theses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group contributions by category and list most recent first
rubrics_metrics.description: Group your contributions by category in the following order, as applicable, listing your most recent contributions first: Refereed contributions; Other refereed contributions; Nonrefereed contributions; Forthcoming contributions; Creative outputs (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the category order and chronological ordering within categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of refereed contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Refereed contributions include books (single-authored, co-authored, edited), monographs, book chapters, articles in scholarly refereed journals and conference proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A “refereed work” involves its assessment in its entirety (not merely an abstract or extract), before publication, and by independent (at arm’s length from the author), anonymous, qualified experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other refereed contributions — examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Other refereed contributions include papers presented at scholarly meetings or conferences and articles in professional or trade journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonrefereed contributions — examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonrefereed contributions include book reviews, published reviews of work, research reports, policy papers and public lectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forthcoming contributions — allowed statuses and details
rubrics_metrics.description: For forthcoming contributions indicate one of the following statuses: “submitted,” “revised and submitted,” “accepted” or “in press.” Provide the name of the journal or book publisher and the number of pages. Do not list contributions not yet submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use the permitted status labels and include publisher/journal and page counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative outputs — examples and evaluation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative outputs may include exhibitions, performances, publications, presentations, and film, video and audio recordings. You may include a website link if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative outputs will be evaluated according to established disciplinary standards and creative and/or artistic merit. SSHRC cannot guarantee links will be accessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other research contributions (non-academic audiences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any other contributions to research and the advancement of knowledge within the last six years, including research contributions to non-academic audiences (e.g., public, policy-makers, private sector and not-for-profit organizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Most significant career research contributions (up to five)
rubrics_metrics.description: List and rank up to five of your most significant contributions over your entire career. The six-year rule does not apply to this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain briefly the significance of the contributions listed; these items may differ from those listed in the six-year sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to training — supervisory and involvement details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on students you have helped train within the last six years: indicate your role in supervising or co-supervising ongoing and/or completed theses, listing these by the student’s level of studies; describe efforts to involve students in your research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify if opportunities for such contributions have been limited because your institution does not have graduate degree programs in your field or discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career interruptions — definition and reporting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Career interruptions occur when researchers are taken away from their research work for an extended period of time for health, administrative, family or other reasons, or reasons related to the COVID-19 pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the optional one-page Career interruptions and special circumstances section to outline interruptions, provide dates, and indicate the reason for the delay in general terms (e.g., illness, disability, family loss or illness, cultural or community responsibilities, socio-economic context, COVID-19). Applicants/co-applicants do not need to disclose personal details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special circumstances — definition and reporting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Special circumstances involve slowdowns in research productivity or any circumstances that impact the progression of academic careers in a distinctive way (e.g., health/disability, administrative, family, cultural or community responsibilities, socio‑economic context, COVID-19; small-institution teaching loads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the optional one-page section to explain impact; quantify impact on research production as best you can (estimates of time or opportunities lost). For example, indicate the amount of time and effort involved in seeking and receiving accommodations to inform committee assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and reviewer handling of interruptions/special circumstances information
rubrics_metrics.description: All information provided to SSHRC is subject to the Privacy Act and will be shared with external assessors and merit review committee members. Merit reviewers are subject to the Tri-Agency Conflict of Interest and Confidentiality Policy and are prohibited from sharing this information outside the merit review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Office Administrators will also have access to your application when submitting on behalf of the administering organization. The information is used to enable equitable assessment of productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify impact of interruptions/special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/co-applicants are asked to quantify the impact on their research production as best they can, providing estimates of time or opportunities lost due to the interruption or special circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing estimates (e.g., time spent seeking accommodations) will help reviewers make an equitable assessment of excellence while taking into account the impact on research production.

rubrics_metrics.name: System removal and deletion behavior for invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: After you have accepted the invitation, the applicant can remove you from the application, or you can remove yourself. If the applicant removes you the invitation disappears from your Portfolio and SSHRC’s database. If you click “Delete,” the system will remove the invitation from your Portfolio and generate an email notifying the applicant that you have deleted the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational note—deleting removes the invitation from SSHRC’s database as well.
